title: RLS escape hatch app.privileged is a plain GUC that the application role can set
resource: current_org_id() / app_is_privileged() policies on every tenant table
affectedTenants: all
exploitability: Requires attacker-influenced SQL executing as crm_app_user (SQL injection, unsafe raw SQL). No such path was found; the queries reviewed are parameterised.
reproduction: As crm_app_user: begin; select set_config('app.org_id','<A>',true); select set_config('app.privileged','on',true); select count(*) from organizations; -> every organization is visible (verified 2026-10-11). Already documented as a limitation in docs/architecture/multi-tenancy.md.
fix: Owner decision. Options, trade-offs and a recommendation (a separate DB role for privileged work) are written up in docs/adr/0028-privileged-mode-must-not-be-a-settable-guc.md (status Proposed). Not implemented: it changes infra and provisioning.
regressionTest: none yet; once the ADR is accepted, a generated check that the normal role cannot reach another tenant even after setting the GUC (fails today by design)

title: 60 of 70 files that lift RLS (privileged()) had not been reviewed line by line
exploitability: The review found three real defects (fixed) and several design notes (TI-011..014).
reproduction: node tools/tenancy-audit/run.mjs --static
fix: All 70 files were reviewed (69 now: scheduled-receipts no longer uses privileged()). 60 reviewed, 2 reviewed and fixed, 7 reviewed-partial (the reviewer could not trace every consumer: platform-store, paygw.store, platform-rbac.store, cms-store, pull-sweep, pull.worker, outbox-drain). A new privileged() call site fails the audit until it is reviewed and listed.
regressionTest: run.mjs ratchet: a new unlisted file fails; partial entries stay visible in the report

title: Manual WhatsApp connect trusts a user-supplied waba_id: the token proves the phone, not the WABA
affectedTenants: any tenant whose WABA id is known to another tenant that holds a valid token for some phone
exploitability: Authenticated tenant with connect permission and a token for its own phone number supplies another tenant's waba_id. Subscribing to that WABA fails but was only a warning. WABA-level webhooks carry no phone_number_id (template status, account updates) and route by waba_id to the newest live connection, so the attacker's workspace would receive them.
reproduction: POST /v2/waba/numbers/connect/manual with a wabaId whose phone_numbers listing does not contain phoneNumberId: before the fix it answered 201 and saved the connection (test 'refuses a WABA that does not list the phone number' failed with the connection payload).
fix: connectManual now requires the WABA to be readable with the token and to list the phone (same rule Embedded Signup already had); otherwise 403 WABA_ID_MISMATCH and nothing is saved.
regressionTest: apps/api/test/e2e/whatsapp-cloud-api-waba/waba-connect.e2e.spec.ts, two tests under 'manual connect' (both red without the fix, green with it)

title: Shopify/WooCommerce webhook_secret selects the tenant but its index was not unique
affectedTenants: none today: the secret is randomBytes(30) generated server-side (newWebhookSecret)
exploitability: not exploitable while secrets stay server-generated
reproduction: n/a
fix: Unique indexes on webhook_secret for both tables. The migration skips an index (with a NOTICE) rather than fail a deploy if a duplicate exists.
regressionTest: applied by every migrate run (verified 292 migrations apply; db:verify-schema 0 errors)

title: security_events accepts inserts from any tenant context, including rows that name other organizations
affectedTenants: log integrity only; reads are privileged-only
exploitability: needs code that writes security_events with a foreign subject_org_id; application code controls that
reproduction: policy text read in the catalog; not exercised
fix: Owner decision. Recommended: WITH CHECK (subject_org_id IS NULL OR subject_org_id = current_org_id() OR app_is_privileged()). Not applied because pre-tenant writers (failed logins) may legitimately name an org without a context and that needs checking per writer.
regressionTest: none

title: market_requests is readable by every tenant, including created_by_org_id
affectedTenants: org ids of requesting tenants
exploitability: database level only; the tenant-facing API does not return created_by_org_id or operator_note
reproduction: grep packages/contracts/src/marketplace
fix: none; classified SHARED_AUTHORIZED in policy/table-classification.json (a public wishlist)

title: Nine CHECK constraints were left NOT VALID by migration 20261017090300_cat_value_checks
affectedTenants: none (data integrity, not isolation)
exploitability: n/a
reproduction: select conname from pg_constraint where contype = 'c' and not convalidated
fix: A migration validates them (SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock, reads and writes continue). A table with offending rows keeps its constraint NOT VALID and a NOTICE names it; the migration cannot fail a deploy. Verified on a fresh database: 0 left NOT VALID.
regressionTest: applied by every migrate run

title: Catalog bridge picked the newest connected device with a number in ANY workspace when called from a worker
resource: NodeCatalogBridge.send (order acknowledgement through the unofficial engine)
affectedTenants: two workspaces that each hold a connected device row for the same number (uniqueness is on channels, not devices)
exploitability: The outbox consumer has no request context, so the lookup dropped its org filter: workspace A's order text (customer phone, order total) could be sent through workspace B's WhatsApp device. Needs the same number connected in two workspaces; not reproduced end to end.
reproduction: reasoned from code and confirmed by the unit test: without an org the old code issued the cross-workspace query
fix: The bridge takes an explicit orgId (the order's), uses the request's only as a fallback, always filters by org_id, and throws when there is neither.
regressionTest: apps/api/test/unit/node-bridge-runtime/catalog-bridge.spec.ts ('fails closed without a workspace', 'always constrains the device lookup')

title: A provider subscription event naming only a plan id was applied to the newest subscription of any workspace on that plan
affectedTenants: every workspace sharing a provider plan (gateway_plan_cache makes one plan per account, price and cadence)
exploitability: Not reachable by a tenant: the webhook is provider-signed. A signed event with neither a subscription id nor an order number that matched would cancel, fail or renew some other workspace's subscription.
reproduction: e2e: two workspaces on one gateway_plan_id, a 'canceled' event with only that plan id -> before the fix it answered 'canceled' and cancelled one of them.
fix: The plan-only fallback applies only when exactly one subscription matches; otherwise the event is 'no_match'.
regressionTest: apps/api/test/e2e/tenancy/tenancy-regressions.e2e.spec.ts (the ambiguous case is red without the fix; the single-match case passes either way)

title: Flow schedule trigger claim updated flows by id only
affectedTenants: two workspaces with a flow of the same id (flows.id is a global identity but only (org_id, id) is the key, so a seeded or imported explicit id could collide)
exploitability: needs an explicit-id insert; defence in depth
reproduction: read from code
fix: WHERE org_id = $1 AND id = $2 AND trigger_last_occurrence ...
regressionTest: no collision test (it needs a hand-made duplicate id); the existing flow-workflow-gaps e2e covers the sweeper's behaviour

title: BillingService.change runs a privileged transaction on a tenant HTTP request
affectedTenants: none today: every statement is keyed by the server-derived ctx.orgId
exploitability: none as written; it breaks the 'never from a request handler' rule, so a future unscoped statement there would be cross-tenant
reproduction: read from code by the reviewer and traced statement by statement
fix: Owner decision. Recommended: a narrow SECURITY DEFINER function (like marketplace_start_trial) or a tenant policy for organizations.plan / org_plan_state writes, so the request path never lifts RLS.
regressionTest: none

title: An operator can copy any workspace's flow into a global starter template by uuid
affectedTenants: the workspace whose flow is copied (nodes, sender ids, message text become readable by every workspace that clones the template)
exploitability: needs a platform operator and the flow uuid; documented in the code as intended
reproduction: read from code
fix: Product decision: keep, or restrict the source to flows the operator's own workspace owns, or strip tenant-specific ids and text on copy.
regressionTest: none

title: Signed public API key guard had no failed-authentication throttle
affectedTenants: none directly; key prefix / revoked-state enumeration with no limit
exploitability: very low: no tenant data, the secret is argon2-verified
reproduction: read from code; the bearer-key guard already had the throttle
fix: 30 failures per minute per address, then 429, shared with the bearer guard through ApiKeyAccessService. Error texts were not changed (documented API behaviour).

title: Delivery receipt lookup relies on provider message ids being globally unique
resource: scheduled-receipts.service.ts lookup by wa_message_id under privileged()
affectedTenants: none known
exploitability: would need two workspaces to hold the same provider message id
reproduction: read from code
fix: The lookup now runs in the reporting device's workspace (db.txAs with the report's orgId, RLS on) and filters by org_id; it no longer uses privileged().
regressionTest: apps/api/test/unit/scheduled-queue-warmer/scheduled-receipts-tenant.spec.ts (never lifts RLS, every statement in the reporting workspace); the device-messaging e2e covers the receipt behaviour

title: No per-workspace request budget: the default throttle is off and the throttle has no workspace subject
resource: INFRA_RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT_PER_MINUTE (default 0), rate-limit.policies.ts subjects ip / actor / actor-or-ip; shared DB pool (max 20)
affectedTenants: availability of every workspace
exploitability: A workspace with many users or API keys can send unlimited requests to routes without their own @Throttle and occupy the shared connection pool. Mitigations that exist: statement_timeout 15 s, per-key API limits, per-route throttles on auth and public routes. The concurrency spec checks liveness of a neighbour during a 150-request burst in one process; it is not a load test.
reproduction: config read; tenancy-concurrency.e2e.spec.ts for the liveness check
fix: Owner decision: set a non-zero default for authenticated routes and add a 'org' throttle subject (a per-workspace bucket), then load-test with k6 on a staging stack.
regressionTest: tenancy-concurrency.e2e.spec.ts (liveness only)

title: Queues have no per-workspace fairness: one workspace's backlog delays the others on the same queue
resource: BullMQ queues (no group or per-tenant limiter)
affectedTenants: latency of every workspace on a shared queue
exploitability: a large broadcast or import enqueued by one workspace; not load-tested here
reproduction: code read: no group or limiter configuration
fix: Owner decision: per-workspace chunking / round-robin enqueue for the high-volume queues, or BullMQ groups, plus a staging load test.
regressionTest: none

title: docker-compose.prod.yml starts Redis with noeviction but no maxmemory
resource: Redis memory in the production compose file (deploy/hostinger sets maxmemory)
affectedTenants: all, if Redis memory is exhausted (writes then fail for everyone)
exploitability: needs unbounded key growth; most keys carry a TTL
reproduction: config read
fix: Owner decision: set --maxmemory to the host's budget (deploy/hostinger uses 192mb in a 256m container). Not changed here: a value that is too low makes BullMQ writes fail for every workspace. Keep noeviction.
regressionTest: none

title: apps/api pins @nestjs/testing ^12 next to @nestjs/common ^11, so every e2e spec fails at import on a fresh install
resource: apps/api/package.json devDependencies (a dependency bump on main)
affectedTenants: none; it removes the executed evidence: all e2e specs (including the authz dynamic suite) error with "Cannot find module .../@nestjs/common/internal"
exploitability: n/a (test tooling). A tenancy or authorization regression would not be caught by e2e while this stands.
reproduction: fresh clone, pnpm install --frozen-lockfile, build the workspace packages, run any apps/api e2e spec
fix: Owner decision: pin @nestjs/testing to the 11.x line that matches @nestjs/common/@nestjs/core (what the audit runs used locally, uncommitted), or move the whole Nest stack to 12. Not committed here because it is a dependency change outside this audit.

title: The outbound-webhooks e2e spec is red on main: its fixture URL is in a range the SSRF guard now blocks
affectedTenants: none; the guard is right, the test data is stale
exploitability: n/a. The spec fails on creating a webhook (422), so its isolation tests cannot be used as evidence and are not counted for any control.
reproduction: vitest run test/e2e/outbound-webhooks/webhooks.e2e.spec.ts -t isolation -> "expected 400 to be 404" and "expected +0 to be 1"
fix: Owner of the webhooks tests: use a fixture host the guard accepts (a public literal that is never contacted, or an injected resolver) instead of weakening the guard.
regressionTest: that spec itself, once its fixture is fixed

title: Tenant API responses carry no Cache-Control, and workspace flow media is cacheable publicly for a year
affectedTenants: none shown: authenticated requests are not stored by shared caches by default (RFC 9111), and nothing tenant-private is marked public
exploitability: A misconfigured CDN or proxy that overrides that default could cache tenant JSON. Flow media is a capability URL (organization uuid plus 96 random bits) served public, immutable, 1 year on purpose, so deleting a file does not recall copies already cached.
reproduction: curl -i a tenant route with a bearer token: no Cache-Control header
fix: Owner decision: send 'Cache-Control: private, no-store' (or at least 'private') on every authenticated route by default, which changes client revalidation behaviour. For flow media, accept the one-year cache or shorten it so deletion takes effect sooner.
regressionTest: tenancy-concurrency.e2e.spec.ts ("tenant responses stay out of shared caches") asserts nothing authenticated is public or has s-maxage

title: One flows e2e scenario errors inside supertest on this machine ("Cannot read properties of null (reading 'address')")
resource: apps/api/test/e2e/flow-builder-editor/flows.e2e.spec.ts, "TW-FLB-022 rule 2/5 ... publish is 404 for another workspace's flow"
affectedTenants: none: the error happens before the final request returns, so its cross-workspace assertion (unpublish -> 404) is not evidenced by this scenario
exploitability: n/a (test infrastructure). The spec's dedicated "permissions and tenant isolation" suite passed 5 of 5 and is what MT-078 counts.
reproduction: run the whole flows e2e spec: 99 of 101 tests pass; this scenario errors in both a filtered and a full run
fix: Test owner: find why supertest sees a closed server for that request (ephemeral-port or listener lifecycle) and make the scenario listen once.
regressionTest: the scenario itself, once stable
